newsitem.title: USA: USDA expects multitude of new crop marketing tools.
newsitem.headline: USDA expects multitude of new crop marketing tools.

text.p: USDA risk management chief Ken Ackerman said Wednesday he expected a multitude of new agricultural marketing tools similar to the controversial hedge-to-arrive contracts to emerge in coming years.
Speaking at a CFTC Agricultural Advisory Committee meeting, Ackerman said the reduction in the government's involvement in agriculture had set the stage for new marketing methods.
"It very likely will create a series of new tools that will appear very quickly," Ackerman said.
One firm was already offering, via the Internet, to buy government seven years worth of farm subsidy payments from farmers at 60 cents on the dollar, he said.

USDA's new Risk Management Agency aimed to use education to give farmers a "level of sophistication" to help them choose among the new array of tools available to them and help them avoid pitfalls, he said.
New contracts known as hedge-to-arrive contracts reportedly have resulted in millions of dollars worth of losses to farmers and grain elevators in the past crop year.

Ackerman said his agency also intended to branch into revenue assurance and to increase the number of crops it insured. Government insurance is currently available for about 60 of 1,000 crops grown in the United States, he said.
He said USDA now insured $25 billion in crops on 200 million acres of land, up from 90 million acres in 1994.
